title: Santal rebellion (Hul)
summary: On 30 June 1855 the Murmu brothers Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand and Bhairav led Santhals from Bhagnadihi village in revolt against moneylenders, landlords and British revenue policies. The rising was put down by early January 1856, with an estimated 15,000 to 20,000 Santhal dead, and it led to the creation of the Santhal Parganas district.

uncertainty.note: Start 30 June 1855 and suppression by 3 January 1856 per the sources; only the years are recorded.

as_recorded.value: The Santhal rebellion began on June 30, 1855 ... suppressed by January 3, 1856

where.historical_name: Bhagnadihi village, Damin-i-Koh region, Bengal Presidency (British India)

importance.justification: A large tribal uprising against exploitation and colonial policy that produced a new administrative district.

audience_note: Describes armed suppression, mass deaths and executions during a colonial-era revolt.

sources.title: Santhal Hul wasn't just the first anti-British revolt, it was against all exploitation
sources.author: Harshvardhan and Shivam Mogha

sources.title: Santhal Rebellion (1855-56): Legacy of Hul and Tribal Resistance in India

reviewer_note: Least sure of the death toll and crowd sizes, which vary by source (Britannica 15,000-20,000; Janata over 15,000 and almost 60,000 mobilised). The village name is spelled Bhagnadihi/Bhognadih; the pin is the Wikidata point for Bhognadih. britannica.com is blocked for automated fetches and was read once only.
